key_facts: **Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS)** is a chronic inflammatory disease of the **hair follicle** in the flexures, not an infection of sweat glands.
Recurrent painful nodules, abscesses, sinus tracts and **rope-like scars** in the axillae, groin, buttocks and under the breasts; **double-ended comedones**.
Diagnosis is clinical: typical lesions, typical sites, recurrence (at least twice in 6 months).
Stop smoking, lose weight, analgesia, topical clindamycin 1%, then a **12-week tetracycline course**; screen for metabolic syndrome and depression.
Refer early for Hurley II–III or failed primary care treatment; biologics (adalimumab, secukinumab) are specialist.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: Chronic autoinflammatory disease of **apocrine-bearing** / intertriginous skin (acne inversa). Painful deep nodules and abscesses that may form **draining sinus tracts** and irreversible scarring. Not caused by poor hygiene; not contagious. Marked quality-of-life and comorbidity burden.

sub: About 1% of people; women about 3× more; starts after puberty, average delay to diagnosis around 7–10 years.
Strong links with **smoking** and **obesity**; a third have a family history.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Follicular **occlusion → rupture →** innate immune cascade → tunnels and fibrosis. Drivers: genetics (~⅓ family history), obesity/friction, **smoking**, hormones, microbial dysbiosis. Female predominance (~3:1) in Western cohorts; onset typically after puberty (2nd–3rd decade).

ol: **Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp** (perifolliculitis capitis abscedens et suffodiens)

blocks: **Tetrad** adds **pilonidal disease**. Syndromic overlap possible (e.g. PASH) — specialist territory.

ul: Follicular occlusion with genetic susceptibility (γ-secretase mutations in familial HS).
Smoking (nicotine promotes follicular plugging), obesity, friction, hormones.
**"It's caused by poor hygiene"**: it is not.
**"Repeated incision and drainage cures it"**: lancing gives brief relief but scars and recurs; treat the disease.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: HS starts with a **blocked hair follicle** that ruptures and drives chronic inflammation.

mech.t: Hyperkeratosis plugs the hair follicle infundibulum in apocrine-gland–bearing skin.
The follicle swells and ruptures, spilling keratin and bacteria into the dermis.
Innate immunity (IL-1β, **TNF-α**, **IL-17**) causes painful nodules and abscesses: the targets of biologic drugs.
Repeated inflammation forms epithelialised **sinus tracts**, bridged and **tombstone** comedones, and rope-like scars.
mech.caption: Double-ended (tombstone) comedones and sinus tracts in HS.

mech.t: Hurley I: abscesses without tracts; II: recurrent abscesses with tracts and scars; III: diffuse interconnected tracts.
mech.caption: Hurley stages I–III.

histo: Not needed for diagnosis. Follicular occlusion, perifolliculitis, abscesses and sinus tracts lined by epithelium.

sections.title: Clinical features

ul: Open/closed comedones (often **paired/"tombstone"**), painful firm nodules, abscesses, **draining sinuses**, rope-like scars.
Sites: **axillae**, groin, inframammary/submammary, buttocks, perianal/perineal, neck.
Typical case: recurrent axillary lumps since puberty → coalescent inflamed nodules, sinus tracts, pus, fibrosis ± smaller indurated nodules.

head: Stage
Meaning
rows: Single or multiple abscesses **without** sinus tracts or scarring
Recurrent abscesses **with** sinus tracts and scarring (separated by normal skin)
Diffuse involvement with **multiple interconnected** sinuses/abscesses across the region

blocks: Once scarring/sinuses exist, Hurley stage does not “step down” with medical therapy alone. Dynamic scores (IHS4, HiSCR) used more in secondary care/trials.
Typical staging: **at least Hurley II** (sinuses + scarring after failed long antibiotic courses).

variants.name: Early nodule
variants.t: Acute painful nodule before tunnels. *Site: Axilla.*

sub: Tetracyclines are avoided in pregnancy; specialist advice on alternatives (e.g. clindamycin, some biologics).
More common and often more severe in people of African descent; scarring and keloids.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Clinical — modified Dessau criteria (typical lesions + typical sites + chronicity/recurrence ≥2 flares in 6 months). Swabs often negative or colonised (supportive if sterile abscess picture). Biopsy rarely needed (exclude SCC in chronic ulcerated anogenital disease). Ultrasound/MRI for extent when planning surgery.

ul: Typical lesions + typical sites + **≥ 2 flares in 6 months**.
Often negative or colonised: supports a sterile picture.
Ultrasound / MRI before surgery; biopsy chronic anogenital ulcers (SCC).
Hurley stage, sites, smoking, BMI, prior antibiotics.

ddx.name: Boils / carbuncles
ddx.f: Discrete pointing abscesses; no tunnels or rope scars.

ddx.name: Epidermoid / Bartholin cyst
ddx.f: Single cyst; no multi-site comedonal disease.

sections.title: Management
blocks: Themes from DermNet and the BAD HS guideline (Ingram et al.):

ul: **Educate:** not infectious, not “dirt”; validate pain and QoL.
**Lifestyle:** smoking cessation; weight management; loose clothing; gentle antiseptic washes (e.g. chlorhexidine) as adjunct; wound dressings that don’t tear skin.
**Pain:** paracetamol/NSAID first-line; escalate thoughtfully.
**Topical (mild disease):** clindamycin 1% BD to active lesions (short adjunct).

**Oral antibiotics (immunomodulatory courses, not one-off “boil” scripts):** tetracycline-class (e.g. doxycycline/lymecycline) often first medical step for mild–moderate disease — typically reviewed ~12 weeks; follow local antimicrobial stewardship.
**Screen comorbidities:** metabolic syndrome, diabetes, PCOS, CVD risk, depression/anxiety.
**Refer dermatology early** for Hurley **II–III**, failed primary-care antibiotics, multi-site disease, or diagnostic doubt — waiting lists are long; do not delay.

blocks.h: Specialist / secondary care (know when to escalate)

ul: Combination **clindamycin + rifampicin** (typically up to ~12 weeks) for more severe/refractory disease — specialist initiation/monitoring (interactions, resistance, contraception counselling).
Other medical: short steroid rescue for flares; acitretin (males / non-fertile females); dapsone; metformin/anti-androgens in selected women — specialist.

**Biologics (specialist only):** UK-licensed options include **adalimumab** (usually first biologic), **secukinumab**, and (more recently) **bimekizumab** — for inadequate control after conventional therapy. Pre-biologic infection screen (CXR, BBV, etc.). Pregnancy plans constrain many options.
**Surgery:** incision & drainage = temporary relief only (almost always recurs); **deroofing**, local excision, or wider excision for chronic tunnels — combine with medical/lifestyle care.

ladder.t: Not infectious, not ‘dirt’; validate pain and QoL. **Stop smoking**, weight management, loose clothing, chlorhexidine washes, non-adherent dressings.
Tetracycline-class course (doxycycline / lymecycline), review ~12 weeks; stewardship.
Clindamycin + rifampicin (~12 weeks), steroid rescue, acitretin, dapsone, metformin / anti-androgens. **Biologics** (adalimumab, secukinumab per NICE TAs); surgery for tunnels.

blocks.title: Prescribing limits and pitfalls
list: **Comorbidities**: Screen metabolic syndrome, diabetes, PCOS, CVD risk, depression.
**Pregnancy**: Intent changes antibiotic, retinoid and biologic choices: ask early.

refer.t: **Hurley II–III**, or failed 12-week tetracycline: dermatology for systemic or biologic therapy.
Chronic non-healing ulcer in long-standing perianal / buttock HS: exclude **SCC**.
Low mood or suicidal thoughts: high psychological burden, support and refer.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Fluctuant abscess with **systemic upset**: same-day drainage.
**Hurley II–III** disease (tunnels, scarring) or failure of a 12-week tetracycline course: refer to dermatology for systemic or biologic therapy.
Low mood or suicidal thoughts: HS has a high psychological burden.
Chronic non-healing ulcer within long-standing perianal or buttock HS: exclude **SCC**.
Chronic pain, odour, depression and suicide risk; impaired work and relationships.
Strictures, lymphoedema, anaemia, fistulae.
SCC in long-standing buttock or perineal disease (rare); associated Crohn's disease, spondyloarthritis, PCOS.
Chronic, relapsing; early treatment and lifestyle change limit scarring. Surgery (deroofing, excision) for persistent tracts.

pearls: Stop calling every axillary lump a “boil” after the third recurrence in the same fold — think HS.
Document **Hurley stage**, sites, smoking, BMI, prior antibiotics.
Pregnancy/breastfeeding intent changes antibiotic, retinoid, and biologic choices — ask early.
Abscess drainage alone is not disease-modifying.

quiz.q: Hurley stage with tunnels and scarring separated by normal skin?

quiz.a: Clindamycin 1% twice daily to active lesions.

quiz.q: Classic clue that separates HS from boils?
quiz.a: Paired (tombstone) comedones, tunnels and rope-like scars in flexures.
